title: Stow a parts box in a lower Systainer, slide the upper Systainer into its rear cleats, and turn T-Loc to connect
instruction: Place the red parts box flat inside the open lower Systainer, close its lid flush, slide the upper Systainer rearward under the lower lid's rear cleats until it seats flush, and turn the lower green T-Loc latch to its connect position so both cases lock together, then let go and move both hands clear.
context: Coupling two Festool Systainer3 organizer cases into one unit requires sliding the upper case 12 mm rearward so its rear base hooks tuck under the lower lid's rear cleats and its front feet drop flush before turning the lower case's 3-position T-Loc cam from open (-55 deg) through closed (0 deg) to connect (+90 deg); setting the upper case straight down perches it 10.8 mm proud on the cleats, and leaving it forward lets the T-Loc cam kick it proud without coupling. First, stowing the red Allit parts box crooked across a divider props the lower lid above 6 deg and blocks stacking. Construction laborers (O*NET 47-2061.00, 1,489,300 US workers: 'Load, unload, or identify building materials, machinery, or tools ...'), carpenters (47-2031.00, 889,700), electricians (47-2111.00, 821,000), and general maintenance workers (49-9071.00, 1,621,800) pack organizer stacks for service vans; Festool's SYS3 page states it 'can be closed, opened and connected with a single turn.'
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the bench; nothing varies by seed, and start positions use removable start pencil ticks (for between-trial reset only, not drawn in the scene). At (34.5, 0.0) cm (within 2 mm and 2 degrees), a light-grey opaque ABS Festool Systainer3 SYS3 S 76 small-parts case (item 577808, 26.5 x 17.1 x 7.6 cm with feet, 7.1 cm body, 25.8 x 16.4 x 6.7 cm interior, 0.40 kg empty; US/EU retail item 577808) rests on its four feet with its 26.5 cm length along y, its rear spine hinge at +x, its interior partitions forming a front-left 9.2 x 10.6 cm cell, its hinged lid propped open against its 62 degree stay, and its front-wall green 3-position T-Loc rotary latch in its -55 degree open detent. At (16.5, 0.0) cm (within 2 mm and 2 degrees), a second closed Festool Systainer3 SYS3 S 76 (item 577808, blue lid identification band, smooth side walls with no side handles, anthracite T-Loc closed at 0 degrees, 0.48 kg with internal partitions fitted) sits flat on the bench ahead of the lower case. At (21.5, +21.5) cm (within 2 mm and 3 degrees), an empty red polystyrene Allit EuroPlus Insert 45/1 small-parts box (item 456300, EAN 4005187563009, 5.4 x 5.4 x 4.5 cm outer, 4.8 x 4.8 x 4.2 cm inner, 14 g estimated, 60 g in simulation; US equivalent: Schaller 2x2x1-3/4 in red plastic box) sits upright on the bench to the left of the cases.
scoring: 0 for good if at any point in the trial either Systainer or the red parts box falls off the bench (more than 30 mm below bench level; on a real bench, checked from the trial video, with the final photo confirming the end state). Otherwise read at the end of the trial. 0.25: the red parts box rests flat inside the lower Systainer (within 5 mm of its floor, tilted at most 10 degrees) and the lower lid is closed flush (at most 2.5 degrees). 0.5: 0.25 met, and the upper Systainer has both rear base hooks slid at least 5.0 mm under the lower lid's rear cleats and sits flush on the lower case (corner seam gap at most 2.5 mm all round, front-to-back offset at most 4.0 mm, side-to-side offset at most 6.0 mm, yaw at most 6.0 degrees, tilt at most 3.0 degrees), without the T-Loc in connect. 1.0: 0.5 met, the lower green T-Loc latch is in its connect detent (+80 to +95 degrees, confirmed on the bench after the 1.0 s hold by lifting the upper case by its sides so the lower case rises with it), both robot hands are at least 30 mm clear of every part, and both cases stay within 2.0 mm and the T-Loc within 2.0 degrees for 1.0 s (20 steps). 0.0: otherwise. On the bench: steel rule or 2.5 mm feeler gauge on the inter-case seam and rear cleat overlap, protractor and end photo on the vertical T-Loc, upward lift of the upper case by its sides after the 1.0 s hold lifting both cases together, and trial video for whole-trial off-bench fall, hand clearance, and the 1.0 s hold.
reset_notes: Between trials, about 35 seconds: turn the lower green T-Loc counterclockwise from +90 degrees through 0 degrees to its -55 degree open detent, slide the upper Systainer 12 mm forward (-x) out of the rear cleats and set it flat on its removable start pencil ticks at (16.5, 0.0) cm (within 2 mm and 2 degrees, closed T-Loc facing -x), open the lower Systainer's lid up to its 62 degree stay, lift the red Allit 456300 insert box out of the front-left cell and place it upright on its removable start pencil ticks at (21.5, +21.5) cm (within 2 mm and 3 degrees), and confirm the lower Systainer sits on its removable start pencil ticks at (34.5, 0.0) cm (within 2 mm and 2 degrees); no consumables are used.
fidelity: Five rigid PhysX bodies (lower tub, hinged lid, 3-position T-Loc cam on the lower front wall, closed upper Systainer with smooth side walls, red parts box) and two hinges with stepped <=40 deg spring drives; zero welds or pose snaps. Rear hooks under lid cleats and three rigid T-Loc cam lobes retain the lid at 0/+90 deg and couple the upper case at +90 deg (holding a 15 N upward pull). Moulded ABS flex, snap-fit partition clips, and loose fasteners inside the insert box are omitted.
